description: Soy Ingeniero Geólogo de Cajamarca, Perú, con gran interés en las ciencias de la Tierra, la geología planetaria y la exploración espacial. Mi objetivo es utilizar ArcGIS y datos abiertos de la NASA para identificar regiones terrestres análogas a la Luna y Marte. Busco desarrollar un proyecto de análisis geográfico y fotografía científica, aplicando mis conocimientos de geología y SIG. Mi participación es individual.
summary:
Planetary Mirrors is a geospatial research project developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 that establishes a comparative framework linking terrestrial geological analogs in Cajamarca, Peru, with target regions on the Moon and Mars.
Focusing on three core study cases, sedimentary (Chota Formation), geomorphological (Contumazá Plateau), and volcanic (Huambos Volcanic Formation) the initiative compares these Earth environments with off-world sites including Slater Plain, Malapert Massif, and Aristarchus on the Moon, alongside Arcadia Planitia, Mount Sharp, and Medusae Fossae on Mars.
To address this challenge, the methodology integrates terrestrial geological engineering with Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Digital Elevation Models (DEMs), and open-access satellite data from NASA missions such as the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) to map relief, slopes, and surface features
. This work is vital because it provides key preliminary criteria for evaluating potential landing sites and future planetary bases, while advancing scientific education (SDG 4) and technological innovation (SDG 9) by using Earth's geology to interpret foreign worlds.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

Planetary Mirrors is a geospatial research initiative that identifies, characterizes, and evaluates terrestrial geological analogs in the Cajamarca region of Peru, linking them directly to equivalent regions on the Moon and Mars13.

The methodology operates across three comparative study cases23:

  1. Sedimentary Case: Chota Formation (San Marcos, Cajamarca)$\leftrightarrow$Slater Plain (Moon)$\leftrightarrow$Arcadia Planitia (Mars)23.
  2. Geomorphological Case: Contumazá Plateau (Cajamarca)$\leftrightarrow$Malapert Massif (Moon)$\leftrightarrow$Mount Sharp in Gale Crater (Mars)23.
  3. Volcanic Case: Huambos Volcanic Formation (Chota, Cajamarca)$\leftrightarrow$Aristarchus Crater (Moon)$\leftrightarrow$Medusae Fossae Formation (Mars)23.

How it works: The project acquires and processes open-access satellite images, Digital Elevation Models (DEMs), and thematic maps to generate unified comparative matrices analyzing elevation, topography, slope angles, surface roughness, geology, and environmental stability across all three planetary bodies3more_horiz.

2. What benefits does it offer?

  • Social Benefits: Promotes scientific outreach and planetary geology education, bringing space exploration closer to students, researchers, and citizens in Cajamarca and Peru7.
  • Environmental Benefits: Facilitates the environmental characterization of terrestrial geological features through satellite remote sensing without needing invasive physical field sampling7.
  • Technological Benefits: Strengthens geospatial analytical capabilities and advances the practical use of publicly accessible planetary and Earth observation datasets78.
  • Strategic Benefits: Delivers preliminary site-selection criteria for assessing safe landing zones, resource access, and terrain suitability for future lunar and Martian exploration bases9more_horiz.

3. What is the expected impact of the project?

  • Community & Academic Impact: Demonstrates how regional geological engineering expertise on Earth can be directly applied to interpret off-world planetary bodies7more_horiz.
    • SDG 4 (Quality Education): Fosters scientific and technological learning714.
    • SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure): Drives geospatial innovation using satellite data714.
    • SDG 15 (Life on Land): Enhances environmental characterization methodology78.
    • SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals): Promotes open scientific data usage and international academic collaboration1415.
  • Space Mission Alignment: Directly supports the scientific objectives of NASA’s Artemis program, the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), and the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO)11more_horiz.

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software were used?

  • Geospatial & GIS Software: ArcGIS 10.8.0 and ArcMap for spatial processing, slope modeling, and thematic cartography6. Canva was used for graphic layout and visual design6.
  • Programming Languages & Frameworks: No custom software framework or code repository was required; the project relies entirely on scientific GIS tools and open datasets16.
    • Earth: SRTM (Shuttle Radar Topography Mission) 30-meter global elevation models17.
    • Moon: LOLA (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter) elevation data and LROC imagery1517.
    • Mars: MOLA (Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter) elevation models, alongside HiRISE and CTX high-resolution cameras from the MRO1518.
  • Hardware: Standard personal laptop16.
  • AI Support: Artificial intelligence tools were used as secondary aids for information structuring, descriptive text organization, and conceptual visual illustrations (clearly distinguished from official NASA scientific data)20.

5. In what sense is the project creative?

The project's creativity lies in using the accessible, real-world geology of Cajamarca, Peru, as a "planetary mirror" to study the Moon and Mars1more_horiz. Rather than viewing local geology in isolation, it establishes a unified analytical framework that transforms Earth's landforms into living analogs for extraterrestrial environments, making space science tangible and accessible7more_horiz.

6. What factors were considered?

  • Geological & Terrain Parameters: Surface elevation, slope gradients, terrain stability, fine sediment presence, volcanic/pyroclastic deposits, and potential water/ice availability422.
  • Landing & Base Selection Criteria: Operational hazards, slope safety, radiation exposure, and geological stability required for human bases9more_horiz.
  • Open Science & Feasibility: Full reliance on open-access NASA and USGS satellite data, enabling high scientific validity as an individual research contribution.
